title: The Health screen lists each backup with its restore-proof state, and not-yet-checked never reads as proven
description:
BROWSER CHILD of task-1f994315fd164a789424349cb7bba4ca, filed by architect-dbe3631e 2026-09-07. That row's own DoD 4 authorises this split verbatim: "If this breaches the file ceiling, split the browser half into its own row named in dependsOn - do not ship a route nothing fetches."

WHY IT BREACHED. I measured the real cost of a daemon read route from the landed precedent rather than from the parent's estimate. task-509c6c16 (`/deployments/health/read`, commit 29f5d723) touched FIFTEEN source files for the daemon half ALONE - the parent row says six. Adding the durable record and the three-state mapping puts the parent at eighteen. The browser half does not fit beside it.

THIS ROW CLOSES THE CONSUMER EDGE, which is the parent's rail 2 ("a producer with no consumer edge is the gap this row exists to close") discharged rather than deferred. The parent lands the route and registers itself in the daemon's own UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES census with a comment naming THIS ROW as the consumer that retires it; this row retires that entry and the UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS entry in the same edit. Both live in `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts` (:129 and :174), so this row edits one daemon test file - that is expected and is how the census is designed to close.

THE ONE PROPERTY THIS ROW EXISTS FOR: NOT-YET-CHECKED MUST NEVER RENDER AS PROVEN. A backup that was written but whose restore check has not run is common - the write is cheap and the check is not - and an operator leans on that difference at the worst possible moment. Three states, visually distinguishable by more than colour, asserted SEPARATELY and by VALUE.

MEASURED AT HEAD 4710d60b (re-measure before planning; global rail 6):
- `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` - every read path is pinned here; a new read without its pin is not reachable in the dev lane.
- `apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts` is the exact-key decoder sibling to copy; the `live-*.ts` directory is the convention.
- `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx` renders the Health screen section and is already wired through `live-environments.tsx` and LiveHealth, so no new mounting is needed - measure that claim before relying on it.
- The parent's served shape is whatever task-1f994315fd lands. Read it off disk; do not restate it here and do not mint a second spelling.

NOT IN SCOPE: the durable record, the three-state mapping, the route and its composition (all task-1f994315fd), and anything that changes what the daemon serves. If the served shape does not carry what this screen needs, report blocked against the parent rather than decoding around it.
definitionOfDone: AN EXACT-KEY CLIENT DECODER beside `apps/control-room/src/live/live-deployments-health.ts` decodes the parent's served frame. It refuses an EXTRA key AND a MISSING key, each with the specific code asserted AND the layer that refused - not merely that decoding failed. A malformed frame fails closed rather than dropping the restore-proof state silently.

THE THREE STATES RENDER SEPARATELY AND ARE ASSERTED SEPARATELY - proven, failed, not yet checked - in the backups list in `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx`, with the state in a `data-` attribute and the three distinguishable by MORE THAN COLOUR (text or shape, so the distinction survives a monochrome or colour-blind reading). Assert each state's rendered output by value, never by a row count.

NOT-YET-CHECKED DOES NOT RENDER AS PROVEN, asserted as its own arm and DRILLED: make not-yet-checked render identically to proven and show the arm goes RED BY VALUE, not by a count. Quote the drill's failing line and its restore proof. This is the row's one safety property; an arm that only counts rows passes the mutation.

A BACKUP WITH NO SHA256 AND NO CHECK TIME RENDERS HONESTLY - absent is stated as absent, never as an empty string, a zero, a dash that reads as a value, or a defaulted 'proven'. Assert the absent case separately from the present one.

THE TWO CENSUS ENTRIES ARE RETIRED IN THE SAME EDIT: the parent's path leaves `UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS` (http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts:129) and `UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES` (:174), and the comment the parent left naming this row goes with them. A separate arm greps those comments, so a half-retirement reds.

NO SECRET, CREDENTIAL, CONNECTION STRING OR RAW PATH THAT LEAKS ONE reaches the decoder, the rendered output, a log line, an error path or a committed fixture (epic rail 3). Assert it on a FAILURE path, with a positive control over a literal containing a credential shape so the arm cannot pass vacuously.

ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (the scheduler package-boundary scan reds on an apostrophe in JSX); confirm any new testid namespace is free before using it, following the sibling section's existing convention.

Gates quoted with their `Test Files N passed` count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test` and `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (this row edits one daemon test file to retire the census), plus `pnpm typecheck`. A bare root `pnpm test` covers NO apps/** file and is not evidence here.
taskRails: NOT-YET-CHECKED IS NEVER PROVEN. That collapse is the entire failure this surface exists to prevent. Assert it by value and drill it.
READ THE PARENT'S SHAPE OFF DISK, DO NOT RESTATE IT. task-1f994315fd owns the served frame, its state vocabulary and its refusal codes. A second spelling in the browser is how the two drift apart.
DECODE EXACT-KEY, FAIL CLOSED. An extra key and a missing key each refuse with a code AND a layer; never drop an unknown member silently and never substitute a default for an absent one.
DO NOT CHANGE WHAT THE DAEMON SERVES. If the frame lacks what the screen needs, report blocked against the parent rather than decoding around it or minting the value client-side.
RETIRE BOTH CENSUS ENTRIES TOGETHER WITH THE PARENT'S COMMENT. Half a retirement leaves a served route recorded as unconsumed while a screen consumes it.
ASCII-ONLY SOURCES, APOSTROPHE-FREE JSX TEXT, dev-proxy-paths pin for the read.

implementationPlan.description: READ THE PARENT'S LANDED SHAPE OFF DISK — no edits, and this step decides whether the row can proceed. At HEAD, record: (a) `git status --porcelain -- apps/control-room/src apps/daemon/src/http` — foreign dirt noted, never reverted; (b) the parent task-1f994315fd is DONE and what it landed — its route module, the served frame's EXACT key roster at every nesting level, its state vocabulary for the three restore-proof states, and its refusal envelope shape(s); read these from the landed source, and DO NOT restate or re-spell them (task rail 2). Measured at planning time the parent was still WORKING with `landing: null` and no backups route existed under `apps/daemon/src/http`, which is why this plan names no keys; (c) `grep -n 'UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS\|UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES' -A6 apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts` — capture the parent's entry AND the comment naming this row, both of which step 6 deletes; (d) `wc -l apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx` (was 178). IF the parent has not landed, or its frame does not carry what DoD 2 and DoD 4 need, call `moe.report_blocked` against task-1f994315fd — do not decode around it, do not default a state, do not mint the value client-side (task rail 4).

THE EXACT-KEY DECODER, copying the sibling's idiom rather than inventing one. New module in `apps/control-room/src/live/` beside `live-deployments-health.ts`, following its shape: an own-enumerable `exactDataRecord` snapshot at EVERY nesting level, module-scoped `LAYER` and `*_RESPONSE_INVALID` constants of its own (the sibling's are `CONTROL_ROOM_DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH` / `DEPLOYMENTS_HEALTH_RESPONSE_INVALID` at :16-17), and a `refusalFrom` covering EVERY refusal envelope the parent's route can actually answer with — the sibling decodes THREE and its comment records that omitting the third is how a store refusal arrives with its cause erased, so read the parent's refusal shape rather than assuming two. Carry the null-vs-unreadable discipline from :159-165: each nested decoder answers null for both an absent and a malformed member, and the raw member is re-checked at the top, so a MALFORMED backup row can never read as an ABSENT one. Do NOT mint distinct codes for extra-key versus missing-key; both funnel to the module's one invalid-response code, which is what task rail 3 asks for.

THE DECODER ARMS, WRITTEN SO THEY ARE NOT ONE ASSERTION TWICE — DoD 1. Both the EXTRA-key and MISSING-key cases will share the module's single code and layer, so asserting `status === "ERROR"` twice proves one thing twice. Each arm asserts the specific CODE and the LAYER (never merely that decoding failed) AND, crucially, that the decode FAILED CLOSED BY VALUE: no partial frame survives, no backup row is returned, and no restore-proof state leaks through. Add an arm per nesting level, since an extra key on a nested backup row is the likelier real defect than one at the top. Add the absent-member arms DoD 4 needs at this layer too: a malformed member must not read as an absent one. Then DoD 6's secret arm — on a FAILURE path, assert that no credential, connection string or secret-shaped literal reaches the decoder's output or its error value, and give it a POSITIVE CONTROL by running the same instrument over a literal that DOES contain a credential shape, so an arm that matches nothing cannot pass as an arm that found nothing.

PIN THE READ AND FETCH IT. Add the parent's path to `DEV_PROXY_PATHS` in `apps/control-room/src/live/dev-proxy-paths.ts` WITH a comment naming this row as its consumer, matching the file's existing entries — its own text records that `/design/read` is deliberately NOT pinned, so a pin is not automatic and its reason must be written. Without the pin the dev server answers the route itself and the screen renders against Vite instead of a daemon. Then wire the fetch in `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/live-environments.tsx` — the file that already imports `EnvironmentsSection` (:10) and renders it (:131), so no new mounting is needed. NOTE the path: it is under `v2/ops/`, NOT under `src/live/` as the row description implies. Feed the decoded frame down as props; keep the refusal path visible rather than collapsing it into an empty list, so a refused read never reads as 'no backups'.

THE THREE STATES, RENDERED AND DISTINGUISHABLE — DoD 2 and DoD 4. Render the backups list in `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/environments-section.tsx` as DoD 2 names, following the file's existing testid convention (`cr.environments.*` and `${testId}.<part>`, :72-112) and confirming the new namespace is unused before taking it. Each row carries its restore-proof state in a `data-` attribute AND distinguishes the three states by MORE THAN COLOUR — text or shape, so the distinction survives a monochrome or colour-blind reading; a CSS class alone is not a distinction a reader can see. Render the absent case HONESTLY: a backup with no sha256 and no check time states absence as absence, never an empty string, a zero, a dash that reads as a value, or a defaulted 'proven'. LINE CAP: `wc -l` the file after the edit — it was 178 against a 250 target; if the list crosses it, extract the list into a sibling module in the same directory and say in the step note that you did and why. ASCII-only source, no apostrophe in any JSX text (task rail 6).

THE SAFETY ARM AND ITS DRILL, PLUS THE CENSUS RETIREMENT. Assert each of the three states' rendered output BY VALUE — the `data-` attribute and the visible text — in separate arms, never by a row count, and assert the absent case separately from the present one. Then DoD 3's drill, this row's whole reason for existing: make NOT-YET-CHECKED render identically to PROVEN and show a NAMED arm goes RED BY VALUE; a count-based arm survives this mutation, which is exactly why the DoD forbids one. Quote the failing line and prove the restore — `git diff -- <path>` empty for TRACKED files, SHA256 equality against an out-of-tree backup for the NEW modules, taken in a call SEPARATE from the restore. In the SAME edit (task rail 5), retire BOTH census entries in `apps/daemon/src/http/http-listener-read-dispatch.test.ts`: the parent's path leaves `UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS` (:129) and `UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES` (:174), and the comment the parent left naming this row goes with them — the file's positive-control arm pins every member named in those comments, so a half-retirement reds.

GATES AND ADVERSARIAL SELF-REVIEW. Each leg FOREGROUND and STANDALONE; read the OUTPUT, not the exit code — no `Test Files N passed` line means nothing ran. Legs quoted with count lines: `pnpm --filter @moe/control-room test`, `pnpm --filter @moe/daemon test` (this row edits one daemon test file to retire the census), and `pnpm typecheck`. A bare root `pnpm test` covers NO `apps/**` file and is not evidence for anything here. Repo-wide legs are a PATH-ATTRIBUTED BASELINE: merge-base failures, HEAD failures, delta intersected with owned paths must be EMPTY; disclose foreign red verbatim, never waive it. Then read the diff as an attacker: can not-yet-checked reach the screen looking like proven by ANY path — a default, a fallthrough, an absent member, a refused read rendering as an empty list? Do the extra-key and missing-key arms assert anything beyond the same code twice? Does the secret arm's positive control actually match its planted credential shape? Did anything client-side derive or default a state the daemon owns (task rail 4)? Are BOTH census entries and the parent's comment gone? Are all sources ASCII with no apostrophe in JSX text? Is `environments-section.tsx` under the line target or extracted with a note? Report every touched path in `complete_step.modifiedFiles`.

comments.content:
PLANNING MEASUREMENT. HEAD, 2026-09-07. One blocking fact, one path correction, one DoD reading worth pinning before a worker meets it.

1. THE PARENT HAS NOT LANDED, so this plan deliberately names NO frame keys. `task-1f994315fd` is **WORKING**, `landing: null`, no `declaredFiles`, no completionSummary, and there is no backups read route under `apps/daemon/src/http` (the only `backup` hits are `activation-read`'s unrelated deferred rows). Consistent with that, neither census entry exists yet: `UNPROXIED_SERVED_PATHS` (:129) is `Object.freeze([])` and `UNCONSUMED_SERVED_ROUTES` (:174) carries only `/budget/commitment/read` and `/documents/ingest`.

Writing key names into this plan would have invented the "second spelling" task rail 2 forbids, so step 1 reads the shape off the landed parent instead. `dependsOn` already gates WORKING claims, so this costs nothing and needs no block.

2. PATH CORRECTION, and the claim it guards HOLDS. The description says the section is already wired through `live-environments.tsx` and asks that it be measured. It is wired — but the file is `apps/control-room/src/v2/ops/live-environments.tsx`, **not** under `src/live/` where the description's neighbouring references point. It imports `EnvironmentsSection` at :10 and renders it at :131, so no new mounting is needed and the fetch-and-feed goes there.

3. DoD 1's "the specific code" IS SATISFIABLE WITH ONE CODE — and that creates the real hazard. Measured: `exactDataRecord` (live-deployments-health.ts:77-97) returns plain `null` for an extra key, a missing key, a prototype mismatch and an accessor descriptor alike, and the module funnels every malformation into one `errored(INVALID_RESPONSE_CODE, LAYER)` (:74, constants at :16-17). Task rail 3 says each case refuses "with a code AND a layer" — *a* code, not distinct ones — so the new module mints its own analogous pair and does **not** grow a per-shape code roster.

The consequence the worker must not walk into: the extra-key and missing-key arms will then share one code and one layer, so asserting `status === "ERROR"` twice proves one thing twice — global rail 1's vacuity shape exactly. The plan requires the distinguishing power to come from asserting FAIL-CLOSED **by value**: after each malformation, no partial frame survives, no backup row is returned, and no restore-proof state leaks through.

4. TWO SIBLING DISCIPLINES WORTH COPYING RATHER THAN REDISCOVERING. `refusalFrom` (:105-123) decodes THREE distinct refusal envelopes, and its own comment records that omitting the third is how a store refusal arrives with its cause erased — so read the parent's refusal shape and cover it, do not assume two. And the null-vs-unreadable rule at :159-165 (each nested decoder answers null for both, raw member re-checked at the top) is precisely DoD 4's "a malformed frame must not read as an absent one", already expressed in this codebase's idiom.

5. THE COUNT-BASED ARM SURVIVES THE DRILL, which is why DoD 3 rules it out explicitly. The three states share a row shape, so a test counting rows stays green when not-yet-checked is made to render as proven. Each state is asserted by value — the `data-` attribute and the visible text — and the drill must red a NAMED arm by value. Same reasoning behind "more than colour": a CSS class alone is not a distinction a reader can see, so text or shape carries it and the test asserts that carrier.

6. LINE BUDGET. `environments-section.tsx` is 178 against a 250 target. DoD 2 names that file for the list, and a written DoD outranks pre-emptive tidying, so the plan renders it there and measures after — extracting to a sibling module only if it crosses, with a note saying so.

planSizeWarnings: Plan touches 8 distinct files (target <=5); plans over 20 are rejected. Small file-disjoint tasks review better and parallelize.

planningNotes.approachesConsidered:

Step 1 reads the shape off the landed parent instead. `dependsOn` already gates WORKING claims on the parent reaching DONE, so this costs nothing.
(2) MINT DISTINCT REFUSAL CODES FOR EXTRA-KEY vs MISSING-KEY. REJECTED after measuring the sibling: `exactDataRecord` (live-deployments-health.ts:77-97) returns plain `null` for BOTH, and the module funnels every malformation into one `errored(INVALID_RESPONSE_CODE, LAYER)`. DoD 1 and task rail 3 say each case refuses 'with a code AND a layer' — 'a code', not distinct ones. Minting a per-shape code would depart from the convention this row was told to copy and would add a layer/roster concern for nothing. See `risks` for what must carry the distinguishing power instead.
(3) PUT THE BACKUPS LIST IN ITS OWN MODULE up front. NOT chosen as the default: DoD 2 names `environments-section.tsx` explicitly, and a written DoD gate outranks pre-emptive tidying. (4) DECODE AROUND A FRAME THAT LACKS WHAT THE SCREEN NEEDS, or mint the restore-proof state client-side. FORBIDDEN by task rail 4; the required move is `report_blocked` against the parent.

planningNotes.risks:
THE TWO MALFORMED-FRAME ARMS WILL SHARE ONE CODE AND ONE LAYER, so they are near-duplicates and one added layer away from vacuous — the exact shape global rail 1 warns about. Their distinguishing power CANNOT come from the code. It must come from asserting FAIL-CLOSED BY VALUE: after an extra key and after a missing key, the decoder yields the failure and NO partial frame — specifically, no backup row and no restore-proof state survives into the rendered output. An arm that only asserts `status === "ERROR"` twice proves one thing twice.

THE ROW'S ONE SAFETY PROPERTY IS A MUTATION TARGET, not a rendering preference. NOT-YET-CHECKED rendering as PROVEN is the collapse the surface exists to prevent, and DoD 3 requires the drill. Because the three states will share a row shape, a count-based arm survives the mutation — the DoD says so outright. Assert each state's rendered output BY VALUE (the `data-` attribute and the visible text), and make the drill red a NAMED arm by value.

MORE THAN COLOUR is a correctness requirement here, not styling: the distinction has to survive a monochrome or colour-blind reading, so text or shape carries it and the test asserts that carrier — a CSS class name alone is not a distinction a reader can see.

THE SECRET ARM CAN PASS VACUOUSLY, which is why DoD 6 demands a positive control: assert the absence of credential-shaped material on a FAILURE path, and prove the instrument works by running it over a literal that DOES contain a credential shape. Without the control, an arm that never matches anything looks identical to an arm that found nothing (`mem:gotcha-a-widening-grep-needs-a-positive-control`).

IF THE PARENT'S FRAME LACKS WHAT THE SCREEN NEEDS, the required move is `moe.report_blocked` against task-1f994315fd — not decoding around it, not defaulting a state, not minting the value client-side (task rail 4). A defaulted 'proven' is the exact failure this row exists to prevent.

HALF A RETIREMENT REDS: both census entries and the parent's comment go together (task rail 5), and a separate arm greps those comments. ASCII-only sources and apostrophe-free JSX text (task rail 6) — an apostrophe reds the scheduler package-boundary scan in a lane this row's own gates never run. Confirm the new testid namespace is unused before taking it.
